engines.label: C i/k/j
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/j/k -> i/k/j with __restrict pointers. Streams B[t][0..n] sequentially across each row instead of striding 512 B down columns, while accumulating each cell in ascending t = 0..k-1 order (-ffp-contract=off). Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 1.21x over the C Track A baseline (0.8971 ms -> 0.7419 ms, 128^3, arm64 macOS).

engines.label: C tiled 32x32
engines.optimizationLog: 32x32 i/j panel cache blocking with the inner k reduction left intact so each cell accumulates in ascending t = 0..k-1 order. Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 0.97x (0.8971 ms -> 0.9250 ms) at 128^3 because the 64 KiB B matrix already fits in 128 KiB L1d while the inner loop still strides B down columns.

engines.label: C i/k/j + SIMD128
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/k/j combined with -msimd128 (-ffp-contract=off). On the baseline i/j/k loop, -msimd128 yields 0.96x because LLVM cannot vectorize the inner t reduction without reassociating floating-point additions. Interchanging to i/k/j makes the inner j loop independent across columns, unlocking 4-wide f32x4 vectorization while every lane still accumulates in strict ascending t = 0..k-1 order (0 ULP deviation, bit-identical). Measured 4.43x over the C Track A baseline (0.8971 ms -> 0.2025 ms).

engines.label: C SIMD128 dot-product (reassociated)
engines.optimizationLog: Explicit wasm_v128 (f32x4) 4-lane accumulation along the inner k reduction in i/j/k order, horizontally reduced via (lane0 + lane1) + (lane2 + lane3). Because each output cell sums 4 partial chains instead of a single left-to-right scalar chain, floating-point rounding differs from the strict-order oracle (max 31488 ULP / 0.002152 relative deviation on full-mantissa LCG inputs, within declared 0.005 tolerance). Measured 1.79x over the C Track A baseline (0.8971 ms -> 0.5021 ms) — slower than c-ikj-simd (4.43x) because gathering strided B elements into a vector register costs 4 scalar loads per step.

engines.label: C++ i/k/j
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/j/k -> i/k/j with __restrict pointers. Streams B[t][0..n] contiguously along rows while preserving ascending t = 0..k-1 f32 accumulation per output element (-ffp-contract=off). Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 1.18x over the C++ Track A baseline (0.8641 ms -> 0.7341 ms).

engines.label: C++ tiled 32x32
engines.optimizationLog: 32x32 i/j panel cache blocking with unblocked inner k reduction. Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 0.92x (0.8641 ms -> 0.9404 ms) at 128^3 where the 64 KiB B matrix already resides in L1d.

engines.label: C++ i/k/j + SIMD128
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/k/j combined with -msimd128 (-ffp-contract=off), enabling 4-wide f32x4 vectorization across independent j columns while preserving strict ascending t = 0..k-1 accumulation per element (0 ULP deviation, bit-identical). Measured 4.29x over the C++ Track A baseline (0.8641 ms -> 0.2014 ms).

engines.label: Rust i/k/j
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/j/k -> i/k/j using bounds-check-free raw pointer traversal. Streams B[t][0..n] contiguously along rows while accumulating each output element in ascending t = 0..k-1 order. Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 1.26x over the Rust Track A baseline (0.9210 ms -> 0.7303 ms).

engines.label: Rust tiled 32x32
engines.optimizationLog: 32x32 i/j panel cache blocking with unblocked inner k reduction. Bit-identical to the strict-f32 oracle. Measured 0.96x (0.9210 ms -> 0.9633 ms) at 128^3 where the 64 KiB B matrix already fits in L1d.

engines.label: Rust i/k/j + SIMD128
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/k/j compiled with -C target-feature=+simd128, vectorizing across 4 adjacent j columns per f32x4 instruction while preserving strict ascending t = 0..k-1 accumulation per output cell (0 ULP deviation, bit-identical). Measured 4.27x over the Rust Track A baseline (0.9210 ms -> 0.2156 ms).

engines.label: AssemblyScript i/k/j
engines.optimizationLog: Loop interchange i/j/k -> i/k/j. The baseline reads B down a column in the innermost loop, touching a separate 64-byte line per iteration; interchanging streams B along a row instead, so lines are fully used and the prefetcher can work. Costs the register accumulator — the running sum lives in OUT, so each inner step is a load/store pair. Bit-identical: for any fixed (i,j) the terms are still added in ascending t with f32 rounding after each add, so no accumulation order changes. Measured 1.28x over the asc baseline (Deno, arm64 macOS, 128^3, 200 iterations).

engines.label: AssemblyScript tiled 32x32
engines.optimizationLog: Classic i/j cache blocking into 32x32 panels; the k loop is deliberately left unblocked so no accumulation order changes. Per-panel working set is 16 KiB of A plus 16 KiB of B against 64 KiB for the whole of B untiled. Measured 1.02x — effectively neutral. At 128^3 the entire B matrix is 64 KiB and already fits in this machine's L1d, so there is no capacity miss for blocking to remove. The tile size is tuned to one machine and this result should not be generalised to larger shapes.

engines.label: Dart / WasmGC -O2
engines.optimizationLog: -O2: -O1 plus minification; documented safe for all programs. Bit-identical to the pinned strict-f32 oracle.

engines.label: Dart / WasmGC -O3
engines.optimizationLog: -O3: -O2 plus omits implicit type checks. Non-default diagnostic mode. Bit-identical to the pinned strict-f32 oracle.

engines.label: Dart / WasmGC -O4
engines.optimizationLog: -O4: more aggressive than -O3 under the same assumptions, input-data sensitive. Non-default diagnostic mode. Bit-identical to the pinned strict-f32 oracle.
